mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.5%) compresses the risk-free rate in equity valuation models, causing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as discounted cash flows increase.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals economic deterioration, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (indicated by slowing industrial production growth), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate economic deceleration.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods classified as late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 3.5%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing immediate negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to liquidity concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS > 137,000 thousand) indicates a strong labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS > 137,000 thousand.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a monetary policy response to high inflation, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime (indicated by GDP growth above 1.0% annualized), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic expansion supports corporate profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods classified as post-recession recovery.
